tips.title: Use a reliable plastic sheet supplier
tips.text: For accuracy and durability, opt for materials from reputable manufacturers like Evergreen Scale Models or Plastruct, which offer a wide range of plastic sheets suitable for scale modeling.

tips.title: Choose the right adhesive for the job
tips.text: Tamiya Extra Thin Cement is a popular choice for gluing plastic parts, but for bonding metal to plastic, consider using a specialized adhesive like Loctite Plastic Bonding Compound or Epoxy.

tips.title: Select a primer that won't compromise paint adhesion
tips.text: Some primers, like Vallejo Surface Primer, are specifically designed to create a surface that's receptive to paint, but be aware that some primers can create a barrier that may require additional preparation or priming again after painting.

tips.title: Source materials from local hobby shops or online retailers
tips.text: Visit local hobby shops like HobbyTown or Michaels, or explore online retailers like HobbyLink Japan or Amazon, to find a wide selection of scale modeling materials and supplies at competitive prices.

tips.title: Store materials in a dry, well-ventilated area
tips.text: Avoid storing plastic sheets or adhesives in humid environments, as moisture can cause warping, bubbling, or degradation; instead, keep them in a dry, well-ventilated area, like a dedicated hobby room or a plastic storage bin with a desiccant packet.
